title: Bassolino 2022 · Chronic stroke hand PPS
citation: Bassolino et al. (2022). Body and peripersonal space representations in chronic stroke patients with upper limb motor deficits. Brain Communications, 4(4), fcac179.
notes: Run one described 110-trial PPS pool. Software uses a generated broadband cue, tactile-channel markers and mouse clicks. The source leaves the allocation of the pool across hands open.

published_method.conditions: Assess the affected and unaffected hand in randomized order, with the participant seated blindfolded and the tested arm supported.
published_method.sound: Three-second broadband looming sound using two physical loudspeakers, one near the tested hand and one 100 cm from the near speaker.
published_method.touch: 100 ms nominal Precision MicroDrives 312-101 vibration on the dorsum of the tested hand.
published_method.count_scope: Supplement does not establish whether this count set covers one or both tested hands.
published_method.response: Respond to vibration within 2000 ms using a foot pedal. Controls use right foot and patients their unaffected foot.
published_method.analysis: Subtract each participant’s fastest mean tactile-only delay from paired RT. Limb grouping in this minimum-selection rule is unresolved.
published_method.companion_measures: Body landmark localization and avatar adjustment are distinct companion outcomes.

reference_parameters.profile_scope: One reported count set of 60 paired targets, 30 silent tactile controls and 20 sound-only catches. The software run uses one operator-selected hand.
remaining_caveats: The supplement does not resolve whether one count set applied to a single hand or the complete two-hand assessment. The software uses one block for the described pool without asserting a published block schedule.
The original 3-second two-speaker stimulus has no published digital asset or gain law. The software uses white noise as a broadband demonstration and illustrative headphone geometry.

The paper gives a 2-second response window and randomized intervals of 500, 750 and 1000 ms. The generator uses toolkit response timing and the reported midpoint interval of 750 ms after the software cue. Exact randomization, original interval anchor and physical response timing are unverified.
The physical motor, foot-pedal response and side assignment require lab verification. Clinical results and limb groupings require the original screening and analysis.
